note: DFA/TABLE-LOOP ROUTE, FLOOR ARM: predicts pcrec-auto-o0 (unoptimized compile) reads WITHIN NOISE of pcrec-auto's own -O2 build on the throughput regime -- the DFA route's hot loop is a table-indexed byte walk (premultiplied-table load, compare, branch), a shape gcc's own scheduling/inlining passes have little to remove even at -O2, so the FLOOR arm should not cost much. Band ±15%, wider than a same-pin cross-testee null-control band has ever been computed for this population (no nullband.py run exists for an -O-level pair; cited as the project's own ±16.62% large-subject-throughput/>=1us stratum ceiling from reports/2026-09-25-capability-0.1-budu-ryzen1600-after-ce658cb7.md, rounded down, since this IS a same-window, same-artifact-source pair and a tighter true floor is expected). A refutation in the SLOWER direction would say the DFA route is NOT insensitive to gcc's own codegen quality after all; a refutation FASTER would be a build anomaly worth its own investigation (an unoptimized build should never beat an optimized one on a hot loop).

DFA/TABLE-LOOP ROUTE, CEILING ARM: predicts pcrec-auto-o3 also reads WITHIN NOISE of -O2 -- same reasoning as P1 (a table-walk loop has little left for -O3's inlining/unrolling/vectorization passes to exploit beyond what -O2 already does), so the DFA route is predicted FLAT across THE WHOLE -O range, not just at the floor. Band as P1.

DFA/TABLE-LOOP ROUTE, SIZE-FOR-SPEED ARM: predicts pcrec-auto-os also reads WITHIN NOISE of -O2 (the SAME flat-DFA-route reasoning as P1/P2 applies regardless of which side of -O2 the level sits) -- pcrec's own [ART-SIZE] size term already competes for emitted BYTES on this route; a size-optimizing COMPILE is a different lever and is predicted to cost nothing extra here because there is little hot-loop optimization for -Os to trade away in the first place.

VM/GOTO-DISPATCH ROUTE, FLOOR ARM: predicts pcrec-vm-o0 reads MEASURABLY SLOWER than pcrec-vm's own -O2 build (ratio O0/O2 > 1.15, a real slowdown beyond P1-P3's ±15% noise band) -- the VM's goto-threaded dispatch loop (tuning.md 2.21's entry-shape rungs; the [OPT-LITSCAN]/[ENG-ISL] lowerings emit straight-line code meant to be scheduled and, where applicable, inlined) is exactly the shape -O0's total absence of inlining/scheduling should cost the most on, unlike the DFA route's table walk. A refutation (flat or faster) would say the VM route's own dispatch is ALSO insensitive to gcc's optimization level, which would argue against spending [B117]'s own charter question further on this axis.

VM/GOTO-DISPATCH ROUTE, CEILING ARM: predicts pcrec-vm-o3 is NEVER MEASURABLY SLOWER than -O2 (ratio O3/O2 <= 1.05, one-sided -- a build that reads FASTER, extra inlining/unrolling helping the dispatch chain, is not itself a surprise and is not bounded below) -- the mirror of P4: if the VM route is where -O0 costs the most (P4), -O3 is the arm most likely to WIN over -O2, since gcc's ceiling tier has strictly more of the same passes -O2 already runs partially. A refutation (materially slower under -O3) would be the "8192 inversion"-shaped surprise this project's own reports/CLAUDE.md caveat already warns readers to check twice before trusting.

VM/GOTO-DISPATCH ROUTE, SIZE-FOR-SPEED ARM: predicts pcrec-vm-os is MEASURABLY SLOWER than -O2 on the VM route (ratio Os/O2 > 1.05) -- gcc's -Os trims exactly the inlining/unrolling passes P4/P5 predict the dispatch loop depends on, trading it for smaller code; pcrec's own [ART-SIZE] size term already competes for emitted bytes on this route (the compilee-side lever this axis adds is a DIFFERENT one, per the configs.toml comment), so a real cost here is the falsifiable claim, not a given.

COMPILE-SIDE, DFA ROUTE: predicts the -O0 .so is LARGER than the -O2 .so on most patterns (no dead-code/constant-folding at -O0), but not by an extreme factor on a table-dominated artifact whose SIZE is mostly premultiplied-table .rodata, unaffected by the compiler's own code-generation quality (only the small code portion moves).
